races.paceDynamic: Arslan, Lincoln Du Seuil, Likealightswitch, Jet To Monte Carlo, Camlin Park, Kentucky Beach and Thankyouforthedays will ensure a fierce gallop from the off in this competitive novice handicap. The early pace will be relentless with multiple confirmed front-runners unwilling to give ground, creating a stamina-sapping test over 2m on yielding to soft ground. Nine horses wanting prominent positions guarantees traffic problems jumping the final two hurdles, where tactical positioning becomes crucial. This punishing gallop strongly favours hold-up horses and those with proven stamina reserves who can benefit from the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the strong early gallop takes its toll on the pace-setters
scenarios.body: The leaders tire dramatically from 3 out, allowing patient hold-up horses with stamina reserves to sweep past the struggling front-runners. The soft ground amplifies the advantage for those saved for one decisive late surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters has the class and stamina to sustain the gallop
scenarios.body: Despite the strong pace, a quality front-runner like Thankyouforthedays or Arslan proves tough enough to withstand the pressure and holds on grimly. Their tactical speed gives them just enough cushion over the late closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not suicidal enough to stop the prominent racers
scenarios.body: Horses like Saveforarainyday or Wackestone get the perfect trip tracking the pace without leading, then strike at the ideal moment approaching the last. They avoid the early speed duel while staying close enough to pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos at the Hurdles
scenarios.trigger: If the congested field leads to jumping errors or interference in the straight
scenarios.body: Multiple fallers or mistakes from 2 out create a lottery finish where the survivors rather than the best horses prevail. Any horse avoiding trouble becomes a major player regardless of running style.

races.paceDynamic: Kai Lung, Moulin Labbe, Proactif and Harwa will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with at least three confirmed pace-setters likely to engage early. The soft ground will intensify the stamina test over this 2m trip, while four prominent runners (Macho Man, Majolique, Adrienne, Michonne) create congestion dangers approaching the business end. This aggressive early pace on testing ground will set up a true staying test that strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce late kicks when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the four leaders go too hard early and crack approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop on soft ground burns out the pace-setters, leaving North Shore and Minella Boss with decisive advantages from their patient hold-up positions. Their closing kicks prove irresistible as the field comes back to them in the final 200 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Proactif or Moulin Labbe can dictate without excessive pressure from the other leaders
scenarios.body: One of the classier pace-setters manages the early fractions cleverly and has enough left to repel late challenges. The Mullins ammunition proves too strong with superior jumping and tactical awareness.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Macho Man or Majolique can avoid the early pace battle while staying close enough
scenarios.body: The prominent runners benefit from a perfect stalking position as the leaders set up the race without getting caught in traffic. Their mid-race positioning allows them to strike at the optimal moment when pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Holds Up
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground fails to take its toll and the leaders maintain their advantage throughout
scenarios.body: The early pace proves sustainable despite four runners wanting the lead, negating the closing kick of hold-up horses. Superior early positioning trumps late rallies in a slowly-run finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems involving Macho Man, Majolique, Adrienne and Michonne when four runners want prominent positions behind the leaders

races.paceDynamic: Eagles Reign is the sole confirmed front-runner and will have an uncontested lead from flag to finish in this 21-runner field. With prominent runners like Timeless Treaty, Fierce Handay, and Hgranca De Thaix content to sit behind rather than pressure the pace, Eagles Reign can dictate moderate fractions throughout the 2m5½f trip on yielding to soft ground. The large field and lack of pace pressure creates a tactical race where positioning becomes crucial over the final half-mile as the field compresses. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late runs, as the sustainable pace and big field will create a sprint finish that punishes early positioning errors.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Eagles Reign sets uncontested fractions and the field remains bunched turning in
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows late runners to close strongly up the rail and wide, with the soft ground aiding stamina over speed. Hold-up specialists with tactical speed can pick off tiring prominent runners in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens from the back straight as prominent runners advance positions
scenarios.body: Timeless Treaty and Fierce Handay can capitalise on good positioning without the energy-sapping closing effort required from the back. Their mid-race moves catch hold-up horses too far back on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Eagles Reign Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the leader maintains strong galloping and the chasing pack fails to organise a sustained challenge
scenarios.body: Eagles Reign exploits his fitness edge from recent Naas second and the 2m5½f trip suits his stamina profile better than shorter distances. The uncontested lead becomes an insurmountable advantage in the heavy conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference or multiple fallers at the hurdles
scenarios.body: The disrupted race flow allows unfancied runners with clear passages to inherit positions as market leaders get hampered. Horses like El Champo with low weights can capitalise on the mayhem.

Several runners making handicap debuts including Healys Pub and potential improvers like Arch Empire returning from breaks
The 21-runner field creates significant potential for interference at the hurdles, particularly affecting hold-up horses who need clear runs

races.name: Rathbarry & Glenview Studs Hurdle (Grade 2)

runners_data.name: Storm Heart
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Townend aboard, excellent recent form on similar ground, perfectly positioned to avoid early trouble
runners_data.comment: Better than ever this season and unlucky not to be closer at Cheltenham (2m5f handicap)
runners_data.spotlight: Triumph favourite two years ago (finished fifth); very lightly raced in the meantime and firmly on an upward curve in winning twice on heavy ground (including a Grade 3) before an admirable third in the 2m5f handicap at Cheltenham (good to soft) where he would have been closer but for hitting two out; top connections haven't got to the bottom of him yet; clear claims.

runners_data.name: Slade Steel
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 8 years old on soft ground after 25 days off, reliable De Bromhead string

runners_data.name: Brewin'upastorm
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but 13 years old is a concern on testing ground despite winning this race previously
runners_data.comment: Previous winner of this race but well into the veteran stage and looks vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race two years ago and returns on the back of finishing second in the Grade 2 National Spirit at Fontwell, a race he'd won twice before; however, he's well into the veteran stage and looks vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Kawaboomga
runners_data.note: Lone leader will dictate terms, 51 days since last run could be freshness advantage or ring-rust worry
runners_data.comment: Eyecatching novice form; should be all the sharper for his belated return at Gowran
runners_data.spotlight: Smart novice who wasn't beaten far by Kopek Des Bordes in a maiden before beating the smart William Munny next time out (on soft); finished behind Storm Heart and Farren Glory in the Grade 3 Red Mills at Gowran (heavy) but ran well after a long absence and he should be considerably sharper here; 3lb better off with Storm Heart.

runners_data.name: The Yellow Clay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying top weight, recent form patchy but has Grade 1 class from novice days
runners_data.comment: Classy novice; going okay when departing three out in a handicap at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: High class novice last season who was second to The New Lion in the 2m5f Grade 1 at Cheltenham; later suffered a heavy fall at Punchestown; this campaign hasn't really got off the ground and departed too far out (three from home) in the 2m5f handicap at the Festival (Storm Heart third) to know how he would have fared, though was going well enough at the time; wouldn't be a surprise to see him get his career back on track.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needs significant luck in running with this pace scenario, consistent handicapper stepping up
runners_data.comment: Admirably consistent handicapper; Jack Kennedy prefers the chances of The Yellow Clay
runners_data.spotlight: Admirably consistent handicapper who didn't run too badly when midfield in the County Hurdle last month; however, this is a step up the ladder for him and regular rider Jack Kennedy evidently prefers the chances of The Yellow Clay.

runners_data.name: Blizzard Of Oz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but Paul Townend's desertion for Storm Heart is a negative jockey signal
runners_data.comment: Still below his best when winning at Thurles; Paul Townend deserts him for Storm Heart
runners_data.spotlight: Got his career back on track on returning to hurdles at Thurles (2m7f, soft to heavy), but that was still beneath his peak form and Paul Townend deserts him for Storm Heart.

runners_data.name: Glen Kiln
runners_data.note: Prominent style and long absence of 71 days makes him fresh but potentially undercooked
runners_data.comment: Appreciated the drop in grade when making all in a Grade 3 at Naas; commands respect
runners_data.spotlight: Better than ever this season and has contested two Grade 1s; appreciated the drop in class when making all in a Grade 3 at Naas (2m, heavy) and this 7yo is a good bet to give his running (stays this far); very sound jumper.

runners_data.name: Grainne A Chroi
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping up significantly in class but 47 days off could help fitness-wise
runners_data.comment: This is more demanding against male opposition and has her work cut out at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Doubled her tally under rules when emerging from off the pace to narrowly win the Grade 3 Quevega at Punchestown (2m4f, soft); this is appreciably more demanding against male opposition and has her work cut out at the weights.

runners_data.name: Farren Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been consistent in defeat but lacks the class of these rivals
runners_data.comment: Held by some of these and last time he was pulled up in a handicap at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Grade 1-winning novice and won over fences last season; hasn't really reached the heights he once promised and was beaten in races won by Glen Kiln and Storm Heart before pulling up in the 2m5f handicap at Cheltenham when tried in cheekpieces (retained).

races.paceDynamic: Kawaboomga will lead uncontested early with five prominent runners (Storm Heart, Slade Steel, Brewin'upastorm, The Yellow Clay, Blizzard Of Oz) creating a wall behind him through the first mile. This congestion will intensify approaching the business end as they fan out for racing room, with hold-up horses Bowensonfire and Grainne A Chroi needing significant luck in running. The pace will be sustainable but not slow given the Grade 2 prize money and quality field. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good early positions and avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will emerge from 3 out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays honest and the prominent brigade get first run on the leaders
scenarios.body: The five prominent runners get ideal pitches behind Kawaboomga and can pick him off in the straight without interference. Hold-up horses get caught in traffic as the field compacts turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Kawaboomga gets an uncontested lead and has enough left to resist late challenges
scenarios.body: The front runner builds a decisive advantage through lack of early pressure and holds on grimly. Prominent runners chase but can't bridge the gap created by the soft going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroics
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to set up the race for closers with clear runs
scenarios.body: Traffic problems dissipate in the final furlong allowing Bowensonfire and Grainne A Chroi to unleash their finishing kicks. The early leaders pay for their exertions on testing ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites become too focused on each other and create openings for unconsidered runners
scenarios.body: Glen Kiln or Farren Glory benefit from tactical errors by the market leaders and sneak through on the rails. The pace collapses allowing a deep closer to emerge from nowhere.

watchPoints.text: Storm Heart and Slade Steel could clash for the same prominent pitch early and compromise each other's chances
Bowensonfire needs the pace to collapse completely or he'll be trapped behind the wall of prominent runners
Kawaboomga's 51-day layoff could see him tie up in the final furlong if the race becomes truly run
The Yellow Clay's top weight burden on soft ground after recent falls could prove decisive late on
Glen Kiln's 71-day absence makes him either primed for a big run or needing the outing badly

races.name: Underwriting Exchange Fairyhouse Chase (Grade 2)

runners_data.name: Energumene
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose age is showing but retains class advantage if Paul Townend can find the right moment to strike
runners_data.comment: Top class in pomp but time catching up with him, held by Found A Fifty on Cork run in Dec'
runners_data.spotlight: High class operator in his pomp; has won eleven chases, including six at the top table; however, it seems like time is catching up with the 12yo and he was well held by Found A Fifty at Cork in December; tailed off at Leopardstown on latest in first-time cheekpieces (discarded); last ran at this trip in 2020; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Front-runner who bounced back well from poor penultimate effort and will ensure a strong gallop from the off
runners_data.comment: Grade 3 win at Naas latest, came up short in this last year, needs to find more to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time chase winner, including two Grade 3s; pulled up in a Grade 3 here on penultimate start but bounced back straight away with a Grade 3 win at Naas (2m, heavy); came up short in this last year when a 7.25l third and needs to find more to feature at the finish.

runners_data.name: Saint Sam
runners_data.note: Natural leader who ran a cracker in this race last year but lacks a recent win despite consistent efforts
runners_data.comment: Runner up in this last year behind Found A Fifty, needs to leave last two efforts behind
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time chase winner but no success since a Grade 2 win at Clonmel in November 2024; ran a cracker in this last year to finish a 0.75l second behind Found A Fifty; below par in both runs this season and needs to leave those tame efforts behind.

runners_data.name: Found A Fifty
runners_data.note: Defending champion who races prominently and has excellent course form but needs a strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Beat Energumene at Cork in Dec', won this last year, pulled up latest but the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-time chase winner; beat Majborough and Energumene at Cork in December; won this race last year, holding off the late challenge of Saint Sam (Blood Destiny a 7.25l third); pulled up in the Champion Chase last time, but this is more his level and he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sa Fureur
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Listed handicap win at Navan shows he handles testing conditions but faces a significant class rise
runners_data.comment: Shaped nicely behind Impaire Et Passe on penultimate, a bit to find on the figures here
runners_data.spotlight: 2-6 over fences; won the Navan Listed handicap in 2024, that Down Memory Lane won last year, off 143, which was his last success; excellent effort in the Grade 2 Red Mills at Gowran in February when a 1.25l second behind Impaire Et Passe; well beaten in the Martin Pipe latest but the return to chasing is a plus; a fair bit to find on the figures, however.

runners_data.name: Down Memory Lane
runners_data.note: Patient tactician who won impressively at Navan in December but unproven at this level and may need more pace
runners_data.comment: Both chase wins at Navan, disappointed at Cheltenham latest, could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Won his bumper here; both chase wins have come at Navan; won a 20.5f Listed handicap chase on testing ground there off 144 in December; disappointed when third-favourite for the Plate Handicap at Cheltenham; better than that and has a good chance at the weights; can't be discounted.

races.paceDynamic: Saint Sam and Blood Destiny will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with both having confirmed front-running tendencies and unlikely to give way easily. Their dual presence guarantees an honest tempo that should stretch the field over this testing 2m4f trip on soft ground. The sustained pace will create conditions where horses need to be traveling well turning for home, as there will be little opportunity for dramatic late swoops. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina reserves who can stay close to the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Suits
scenarios.trigger: If Saint Sam and Blood Destiny engage early and maintain a strong gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The relentless pace will find out any stamina deficiencies and favour horses who can race prominently without excessive early effort. Those positioned handy to the speed will have first run on the leaders when they begin to tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders get away with softer fractions than expected
scenarios.body: Saint Sam and Blood Destiny could have enough left to hold off late challengers, particularly with their proven stamina over this trip. The defending champion Found A Fifty may not get the strong pace needed to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Sa Fureur and Down Memory Lane could benefit from their patient tactics if given too much rope by the leaders. Their closing kicks would be more effective over a shortened home straight battle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If Energumene recaptures his old brilliance despite recent form concerns
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old's class could shine through if Paul Townend times his challenge perfectly from his prominent position. His superior grade of form gives him a puncher's chance if the pace sets up right.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny and Saint Sam battle too hard early and set it up for Found A Fifty to repeat last year's victory
Energumene travels ominously well turning for home despite his advancing years and recent disappointing efforts
Sa Fureur gets the strong pace his hold-up style requires but may find this Grade 2 company too hot
Down Memory Lane's Navan form translates to this higher grade if the race develops into his favoured scenario
Found A Fifty struggles to repeat last year's performance if the front-runners get away with easier fractions

races.name: BOYLE Sports Irish Grand National Chase (Extended Handicap Chase) (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: The Jukebox Kid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer facing severe traffic problems with 12 others wanting that position
runners_data.comment: 3-4 over fences, a good jumper with considerable potential for improvement, strong chance
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner in 2024; won on the first of two starts over hurdles last season; made winning chase debut at Carlisle in November; suffered a reverse at Cheltenham before making amends with two 3m Ascot wins, in a handicap and the Grade 2 Reynoldstown; good jumper with considerable potential for improvement,

runners_data.name: Better Days Ahead
runners_data.note: Proven Grade 2 winner whose prominent style could benefit from good positioning
runners_data.comment: Sixth in this last year, rider's valuable 7lb claim eases burden, one of six for Elliott
runners_data.spotlight: Won two small-field chases (including a Grade 2) at Navan last season and third in the Brown Advisory; faded from three out when sixth behind Haiti Couleurs in this race last year; ran in two small-field races at Navan in February; rider's claim takes some of the sting from his hefty burden; one of six for the stable.

runners_data.name: Kiss Will
runners_data.note: Front-runner who needs to avoid setting unsustainable pace against two other leaders
runners_data.comment: Still a maiden after four runs over fences, potential for improvement, Paul Townend rides
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdles form comprised 2m/3m wins (including Listed) either side of a comprehensive defeat in the Turners at the 2025 Cheltenham Festival; still a maiden after four runs over fences; decent placed form linked to Flicker Of Hope and Soldier In Milan; faded from the last when fifth (third best of yard's runners) in the Jack Richards at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Monbeg Genius
runners_data.note: Experienced prominent racer with solid form at this trip and going
runners_data.comment: Had all but one of the Irish raiders behind when a fine third in the Kim Muir, respected
runners_data.spotlight: Third in the Ultima at Cheltenham (3m1f, soft) in March 2023; in good form this season; ran respectably in the Welsh National (3m6f, good to soft) and Haydock Grand National Trial (3m4f, good to soft); had all but one of the Irish challengers behind when a fine third in the Kim Muir.

runners_data.name: Kurasso Blue
runners_data.note: Progressive young chaser whose prominent style faces congestion concerns
runners_data.comment: Jumped badly and pulled up four out when 7-2 second favourite for the National Hunt Chase
runners_data.spotlight: 2-3 over hurdles; saw off useful opposition at Punchestown (2m7f, heavy) in December in his second chase; runner-up to Flicker Of Hope at Naas (almost 3m1f, soft) in January; jumped badly and pulled up four out when 7-2 second favourite for the National Hunt Chase; cheekpieces on now.

runners_data.name: Soldier In Milan
runners_data.note: Natural leader who must avoid pace duel with Kiss Will and O'Toole
runners_data.comment: Beat Kiss Will over 2m7f at Punchestown, has to reverse Thurles form with C'Est Ta Chance
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner in 2024; bumper winner at Punchestown last April (2m3f, yielding); clinically abnormal when pulled up on chasing debut; not beaten far in fourth behind C'Est Ta Chance at Gowran (2m4f, heavy) in January; game winner from Kiss Will over 2m7f at Punchestown; fairly tame effort behind C'Est Ta Chance at Thurles; could bounce back to produce a big run.

runners_data.name: The Enabler
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from in-form Elliott yard but faces positioning battle
runners_data.comment: Weakened in the last half-furlong of the Kim Muir, that raises a doubt about his stamina
runners_data.spotlight: Impressed with a 15l win over 2m5f at this venue in December on second chase start; two lesser runs followed in Grade 3 races; travelled well for a long way in the Kim Muir before weakening in the last half-furlong; that raises a doubt about his stamina.

runners_data.name: O'Toole
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner adding to pace pressure from the start
runners_data.comment: Won a Listed handicap chase over an extended 2m5f at Leopardstown last time, stays 3m-plus
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly-raced 10yo whose initial chase win came in a 2m4f Newcastle handicap in 2023; more recently won a 3m1f Ayr handicap hurdle early last year; seasonal return over fences at Cork in November was encouraging; bounced back from a poor Haydock run when winning a Listed handicap chase over an extended 2m5f at Leopardstown.

runners_data.name: Weveallbeencaught
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly suited to expected strong gallop scenario
runners_data.comment: Second in Munster National, a bit to find with Monbeg Genius on running in the Kim Muir
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort this season when second in the Munster National in October (3m, yielding to soft); has a bit to find with Monbeg Genius on running in the Kim Muir (finished seventh), but closely matched with The Enabler and Waterford Whispers on that showing.

runners_data.name: One Big Bang
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who handles soft ground well
runners_data.comment: Lively display when third in the 3m6f National Hunt Chase on handicap debut, good chance
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth in last year's Pertemps Final and ended the season with a creditable third in a handicap hurdle at the Punchestown festival; this season's chase win came in a match at Southwell and he had run only in small-field races over fences until a lively display to take third place in the 3m6f National Hunt Chase on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Western Walk
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose style matches race shape but inexperienced over fences
runners_data.comment: Decent hurdler at up to 3m (rated 132), yet to win over fences, handicap debut off 135
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful hurdler at up to 3m (rated 132); yet to win over fences, but not disgraced in Grade 1 behind Final Demand at Limerick in December; third behind two smart types in Navan Grade 2 at Navan; kept ticking over with a hurdles run last month.

runners_data.name: Velvet Elvis
runners_data.note: Former Thyestes runner-up whose recent form is concerning
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in the Troytown on stable debut and has continued to struggle, faces huge task
runners_data.spotlight: Peak form includes a clear second to subsequent Grand National winner Nick Rockett in Thyestes Chase at Gowran (3m1f, soft to heavy) for Gavin Cromwell last season; pulled up in the Troytown on stable debut and has continued to struggle; failed to take to the cross-country course at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Waterford Whispers
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form for De Bromhead stable
runners_data.comment: Failed to run to expectations in the Kim Muir, unwise to discount, trainer's sole runner
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the Martin Pipe Handicap Hurdle in 2024; 0-7 over fences but he returned to form when third in a big-field handicap at Leopardstown (extended 2m5f, soft) in February; failed to run to expectations in the Kim Muir (9-2 chance), but unwise to discount; trainer's sole runner.

runners_data.name: C'Est Ta Chance
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse from Mullins yard with stamina to burn
runners_data.comment: Confirmed Gowran form with Soldier In Milan when landing a Grade 3 event at Thurles
runners_data.spotlight: Achieved a peak rating of 135 over hurdles; midfield when beaten 20l on chase debut at this venue; little impression when beaten almost 30l in fourth at Leopardstown; much improved when beating two shorter-priced stablemates at Gowran; confirmed the form of that race with Soldier In Milan when landing a Grade 3 event at Thurles.

runners_data.name: Shecouldbeanything
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer returning after 74-day break for Elliott
runners_data.comment: Creditable third in the Thyestes despite a couple of sluggish jumps, Jack Kennedy aboard
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins last season included 2m4f Grade 3 Tipperary novice; also finished third to Dinoblue at Cheltenham; reappeared with a fine third in the Galway Plate in July; pulled up in Kerry National, two veterinary excuses offered; managed a creditable third in the Thyestes despite a couple of sluggish jumps; Jack Kennedy aboard.

runners_data.name: Shanbally Kid
runners_data.note: Long-distance specialist whose Punchestown win came over 3m7f
runners_data.comment: 3m7f Punchestown winner, needs to jump better than when fourth in the Leinster National
runners_data.spotlight: Came good over fences at last year's Punchestown festival in a 23-runner extended 3m7f handicap, winning by 15l; took a hefty 14lb rise for that; never dangerous on seasonal return at Leopardstown and pulled up in the Thyestes; needs to jump better than when fourth in the Leinster National.

runners_data.name: Rushmount
runners_data.note: Amateur ridden hold-up horse better suited to easier company
runners_data.comment: Back in his comfort zone after an ambitious Brown Advisory run, one of three for stable
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins at Thurles; improved to win a handicap there (extended 2m5f, yielding) in December; form has worked out well; back in his comfort zone after an ambitious run in the Brown Advisory.

runners_data.name: Sa Majeste
runners_data.note: Struggled this season until recent third suggests return to form
runners_data.comment: Definite signs of a return to form when third in the 3m1f Leinster National at Naas
runners_data.spotlight: Dual chase winner last term and ran a fine race in the Kim Muir over 3m2f at Cheltenham; pulled up in this last year, and struggled this season until showing definite signs of a return to form when third in the 3m1f Leinster National at Naas last month.

runners_data.name: Search For Glory
runners_data.note: Heavyweight prominent racer who was going well when unseating at Cheltenham
runners_data.comment: Good form before Thyestes flop, disputing lead when unseating at the last in the Ultima
runners_data.spotlight: Disputing the lead when unseating at the last in the Ultima at Cheltenham, a fine effort against the background of his failure (pulled up) in the Thyestes at Gowran; if none the worse for his Cheltenham experience, has a clear chance on his second placing in the Paddy Power Chase at Leopardstown (3m, yielding).

runners_data.name: Flicker Of Hope
runners_data.note: Smart hold-up chaser perfectly suited to strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Good winner at Naas in January, flopped in a race won by Argento Boy at  the same venue
runners_data.spotlight: Smart hurdler who has taken really well to chasing; won a 2m4f beginners' event at this venue (heavy) and relished step up to an extended 3m at Naas when outstaying odds-on favourite Kurasso Blue on soft in January; flopped in a Grade 3 won by Argento Boy at the same venue later that month.

runners_data.name: Karia Des Blaises
runners_data.note: Young hold-up horse claimed by 7lb apprentice

runners_data.name: Showurappreciation
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse with three straight wins under his belt
runners_data.comment: Maintained progression in winning at Navan last month, definite chance despite 9lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well on handicap chase debut at Navan when third to The Lovely Man (3m, soft to heavy); built on that when winning at Punchestown (2m7f, soft to heavy); took advantage of his lower hurdles mark on his next start; maintained progression in winning a valuable novice handicap at Navan; may remain competitive under a 9lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Duffle Coat
runners_data.note: Out of form for 194 days and facing stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: 1-18 over fences, out of form since second in the 2024 Galway Plate, hard to make a case
runners_data.spotlight: 1-18 over fences; out of form since second in the 2024 Galway Plate; 50-1 when pulled up in last year's edition of this race; trainer has stronger candidates.

runners_data.name: Argento Boy
runners_data.note: Recent Grade 3 winner whose prominent style faces traffic concerns
runners_data.comment: Smart novice, ground too lively for him in the Brown Advisory, one of seven for Mullins
runners_data.spotlight: Made amends for a fall on his chasing debut with wins in a beginners' event at Punchestown in December and Naas Grade 3 in January (extended 3m, heavy); struggled in the Brown Advisory (won by stablemate Kitzbuhel) on ground that was probably too lively; one of seven for the stable.

runners_data.name: Joystick
runners_data.note: Improved chaser stepping up significantly in class from last win
runners_data.comment: Not attractively handicapped, 15lb higher than hurdles mark, yard has better candidates
runners_data.spotlight: Big improvement on third chase start when beating Slade Steel at Navan (3m, soft to heavy) in January; out of his depth in the Brown Advisory; 15lb higher than his hurdles mark, not attractively handicapped; tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Goraibhmaithagat
runners_data.note: Novice hold-up horse making just his fourth chase start
runners_data.comment: Just run out of it in the 3m1f Leinster National, perhaps not sure to stay this far

runners_data.name: Yeah Man

runners_data.name: Born Braver

runners_data.comment: Appreciated better ground when landing the 3m4f Ulster National, has an 8lb penalty

runners_data.name: Better Times Ahead
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse who won the Porterstown Chase here in December
runners_data.comment: Maintained progression when second in the Thyestes, kept ticking over with a hurdles run
runners_data.spotlight: In top form this season, won a handicap hurdle off 108 at this venue in November; followed up by beating Will Do narrowly in the Porterstown Chase here in December (3m6f, yielding to soft); left in the lead at the final fence in the Thyestes before being overhauled by Now Is The Hour (3m1f, heavy); probably found 2m3f inadequate over hurdles on latest.

runners_data.name: Hartur d'Arc
runners_data.note: Completely out of form with no recent encouraging signs
runners_data.comment: Down the field in the Paddy Power at Leopardstown, out of form over hurdles more recently
runners_data.spotlight: Finished second in last year's Leinster National at Naas; completely out of form over hurdles on his last two starts, previously down the field in the Paddy Power at Leopardstown.

races.paceDynamic: Soldier In Milan, Kiss Will and O'Toole will ensure a strong gallop from the start in this 30-runner marathon. With 12 prominent racers including The Jukebox Kid, Better Days Ahead, Monbeg Genius and Kurasso Blue fighting for position, expect severe traffic problems from the home turn onwards. The relentless pace combined with soft ground will stretch the field dramatically over the final mile. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early congestion and produce late sustained runs when the pace setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the strong pace and prominent congestion plays out as expected
scenarios.body: The early gallop will stretch the field and create gaps for patient riders, while prominent runners get caught in traffic or pay for early exertions. Late-running stamina horses like C'Est Ta Chance, Flicker Of Hope and Western Walk can pick off weakening leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent survivor strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can secure a good position and avoid trouble
scenarios.body: A horse like Better Days Ahead or Monbeg Genius gets first run on the leaders and has enough left to hold off the closers. The strong pace still helps but they benefit from tactical positioning rather than pure stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses early
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too hard and fade before halfway
scenarios.body: Without sustained pressure, the race becomes a sprint finish favouring horses with tactical speed over pure stamina. Prominent racers who conserved energy can outkick the hold-up horses in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays
scenarios.trigger: If Kiss Will or Soldier In Milan can control the tempo and last home
scenarios.body: A shrewd front-running ride manages to string out the field without going suicidally fast, keeping enough in reserve to resist late challenges. This requires perfect judgment and a career-best performance.

races.paceDynamic: Prophet's Corner is the only confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field, meaning he can dictate terms without pressure from the flag. With most runners holding prominent or midfield positions, the pace will build gradually through the early stages before intensifying from three out. The lack of early pace pressure will create a strong gallop that suits horses with tactical speed who can position handily and kick when it matters. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can travel well in behind before producing a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Benefits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Prophet's Corner maintains a decent gallop throughout without being harried
scenarios.body: The even tempo allows prominent runners to stay in touch without over-racing, setting up a tactical finish where positioning and a turn of foot matter most. Those tracking the pace can time their challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Favours Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Prophet's Corner goes too steady early and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows hold-up horses to get closer than usual, and their superior finishing kick becomes decisive in a cavalry charge finish. Late closers can swamp the early leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Tests Stamina
scenarios.trigger: If the large field and testing ground create a truly run race throughout
scenarios.body: The combination of soft ground and sustained pace becomes a test of pure staying power over the extended trip. Those with proven stamina reserves and course form come to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Prophet's Corner gets headed early or the pace becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: The irregular tempo disrupts timing and creates a scrambled finish where luck in running and jockey skills become paramount. Unexposed types or those due a change of fortune can capitalize.

races.paceDynamic: Jeroboam Machin, Charismatic Kid, Soul Asylum and Poetisa will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with multiple confirmed front-runners creating sustained pressure throughout. The strong pace will test stamina reserves over 2m on yielding to soft ground, particularly punishing horses that race too keenly early. This race shape will heavily favour hold-up horses and patient rides, as the early speed merchants are likely to pay for their exertions in the final furlong. The tactical advantage clearly lies with horses that can settle off the pace and deliver late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners go too hard early and falter in the final 2f
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will set up perfectly for late closers with stamina, as the pace-setters pay for their early exertions. Hold-up horses with tactical speed will sweep past tired leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate fractions and kick clear when rivals weaken
scenarios.body: Jeroboam Machin or Charismatic Kid could use their class advantage to control the race and maintain enough in reserve. Their superior ratings give them the edge if they can get first run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Upsets Field
scenarios.trigger: If Big Boy Dan or Queen Alice produce debut performances to match their breeding
scenarios.body: The newcomers could benefit from having no exposed form while others have shown their limitations. Fresh legs and untapped potential might overcome the proven performers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners maintain their gallop without weakening significantly in the closing stages
scenarios.body: The leaders would need to be exceptionally fit and the ground not as testing as expected for this to occur. Only the highest-rated pace-setters could sustain such an effort.
